transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-20
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Johnson (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), James Lee (Acme CTO), Maria Gonzalez (Acme SRE), Tom Wu (Acme ML), Olivia Park (Acme PM)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Discussed POC scope for benchmark integration, customer scripts, load testing windows, streaming vs non-streaming scenarios, success criteria (latency/throughput/quality), security access for harness, and timelines for a short pilot. Agreed to share harness template and schedule tests.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Johnson: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, we got James, Maria, Tom, Olivia on the customer side and Priya and Liam from our side, uh hi all.
[00:18] James Lee: hey Alex, yep, thanks. quick context: we're trying to validate inference economics and latency for a triage assistant for clinicians, so it's quite sensitive to both latency and accuracy.
[00:34] Priya Nair: great, thanks James. so for today's session we want to scope the POC benchmarks — like what workloads you'll run, the harness integration, and the streaming vs non-streaming tests. also make sure success criteria and timeline are clear.
[00:51] Maria Gonzalez: yeah, from infra we care about concurrency, total QPS, and also whether we need dedicated for predictable tail latency. we also need to validate data residency and KMS integration.
[01:07] Tom Wu: and from ML we care about quality regression versus your current model; we'll bring our reference prompts and test set. also we have some legacy scripts in locust and a small wrapper around python asyncio for streaming.
[01:24] Alex Johnson: perfect. just to set expectations: our benchmark harness supports both synthetic load (wrk/locust) and trace-replay using your scripts. we can run streaming (chunked/stream responses) and non-streaming (complete response) modes. we'll help integrate your scripts into the harness.
[01:40] Liam Ortiz: one note — sometimes the transcription in our docs says Redwood Dedicated as Red wood Dedicated, ignore that — but dedicated mode gives you reserved capacity, which helps p95/p99.
[01:53] Olivia Park: timeline-wise, we want results within two weeks if possible. is that feasible?
[02:01] Priya Nair: yeah two weeks is doable if we get the representative workloads and scripts this week. ideal flow: customer shares scripts + sample dataset, we onboard them into the harness, run baseline tests on hosted (sanity) and then run the full load tests on a dedicated setup (or emulated config), compare p50/p95/p99 and cost, and evaluate streaming impacts.
[02:23] James Lee: for success criteria: p95 latency under 400ms for short prompts (<128 tokens), throughput of 100 req/s sustained with concurrency 40, and quality match within 2% of our baseline nlg metric. correct summary?
[02:38] Priya Nair: yes that's a good starting point. we typically ask for both token-latency (per-token generation) and end-to-end latency. for streaming we'll also capture first-byte latency and time-to-first-token which matters for UX.
[02:53] Maria Gonzalez: how do you handle KV cache across sessions? our use case relies on reuse of conversation context to reduce compute.
[03:00] Priya Nair: we have KV cache support in the runtime and the harness can simulate cache hits vs cold starts. we can run a test matrix: cold-start only, warm cache (repeated sessions), and mixed traffic. that will show realistic per-token cost and latency improvements.
[03:18] Tom Wu: for my scripts, they do streaming via an internal websocket shim; can Redwood's harness replay websocket traffic or do we need to adapt?
[03:27] Alex Johnson: good question. we support two integration patterns: 1) you run our harness and point to your streaming endpoint, or 2) you provide client-side generator scripts and we adapt them into the harness runner (we have a small shim that accepts async generators). sometimes small modifications are needed — we can help.
[03:43] James Lee: security — we need SOC 2, SSO, audit logs, and also KMS for key management. do you have those in a POC?
[03:52] Liam Ortiz: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and SSO/SAML integrations are available. for the POC we can provide scoped audit logs and a limited KMS integration demo; production-grade keys require provisioning but we can simulate. we'll attach our security playbook.
[04:09] Olivia Park: any blockers on your side for us sharing scripts and a small sample dataset? we can sanitize PHI.
[04:15] Maria Gonzalez: we'll sanitize and share a 1000-record sample and our locust scripts by Friday.
[04:21] Alex Johnson: perfect. then next we'll onboard the scripts into our harness. quick question on targets — do you have a preferred benchmark tool? we support locust, wrk, and custom python runners.
[04:33] Tom Wu: locust is fine since we already use it, plus some simple python async wrappers.
[04:38] Priya Nair: good — we'll take your locust scenarios and convert them into harness jobs. which brings up streaming vs non-streaming: we typically recommend doing both. streaming for UX (lower time-to-first-token) and non-streaming for throughput/cost numbers.
[04:55] James Lee: can you quantify the difference — like what to expect for streaming overhead?
[05:00] Priya Nair: streaming has slightly higher per-request signaling overhead but often lower perceived latency because you get the first token fast. non-streaming can be more efficient for batch scenarios. we'll capture both metrics: CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens.
[05:14] Maria Gonzalez: also please show us how quantization changes numbers. we might try int8 quant and see inference speedups.
[05:20] Liam Ortiz: yes, we'll include quantized variants where supported. note some models trade accuracy for int8 gains; we'll include quality regressions in the matrix.
[05:31] Alex Johnson: ok let's map out the benchmark matrix live: dimensions — model variant, streaming vs non-streaming, warm vs cold cache, concurrency/QPS sweep, and quantization profile. we should prioritize a smaller matrix first to hit your two-week timeline.
[05:46] James Lee: prioritization: 1) production model (our current checkpoint) non-streaming cold vs warm, 2) streaming on same model to measure time-to-first-token, 3) int8 variant to check cost/quality. does that sound right?
[06:01] Priya Nair: yes. we can run baseline tests on hosted to sanity-check then spin dedicated nodes for the heavy concurrency sweeps. for the dedicated config, do you have GPU preferences? A100 vs H100?
[06:13] Tom Wu: we have some H100 instances in our infra team but cost is a factor; for POC we want to test on a mid-range GPU that matches expected production. maybe A10 or A30?
[06:24] Alex Johnson: we can emulate with our internal fleet; we'll try to match memory & throughput. if you want exact H100 numbers we can arrange a run but that might add scheduling time.
[06:35] Olivia Park: scheduling time — how much lead time to run full sweeps on dedicated?
[06:40] Priya Nair: typically 2–3 business days to provision and validate, then 24–48 hours of runs depending on matrix size. so plan for about a week total from when we have scripts and access.
[06:52] James Lee: okay that's okay. about success criteria — aside from latency and throughput what about quality thresholds? we said within 2% relative to baseline, but what's the metric? F1? bertscore?
[07:03] Tom Wu: for summarization/triage we use an NLG BLEU-ish composite and a clinical recall metric. we'll provide the scripts to compute metrics.
[07:13] Priya Nair: excellent — please include the metric scripts in the repo so we can run them after each candidate run and produce a regression report.
[07:20] Maria Gonzalez: on the harness integration: will you run tests from within our VPC or from Redwood's hosted infra?
[07:27] Liam Ortiz: two modes: 1) we run from Redwood-hosted test runners hitting either your hosted endpoints or our endpoint; or 2) we can deploy the harness into your VPC via a short-lived k8s job or a docker runner. the latter is preferred for network parity.
[07:44] Maria Gonzalez: good. for security we'd prefer VPC-local tests.
[07:47] Alex Johnson: we'll provide helm chart / docker image and a README. Priya will drop a sample k8s job.
[07:54] Olivia Park: what about tracing & observability during runs? we want per-request traces and token breakdown + cost.
[07:59] Priya Nair: our observability collects per-route latency histograms, token counts, cost estimates, and aggregates by model. we can stream logs to your S3 or push to your splunk/df.
[08:11] James Lee: excellent. a couple of nitty gritty questions: 1) does the harness simulate real user think-time and session stickiness? 2) how do you capture streaming websockets?
[08:21] Alex Johnson: 1) yes, load profiles support think-times and session affinity. 2) for websockets we support replay via a small shim; sometimes we ask customers to run their streaming shim inside the harness container for best fidelity.
[08:33] Tom Wu: about result artifacts — will you provide raw logs + summary dashboards?
[08:38] Priya Nair: yes raw logs, consolidated CSVs, and a summary dashboard with plots for latency/throughput/token-cost/quality regression. we'll also give a short findings doc.
[08:48] Maria Gonzalez: any limitations we should know? e.g. large context windows >8k tokens?
[08:54] Liam Ortiz: we support various context sizes but very large windows increase memory pressure; we'll call out memory/seq length constraints per model. if you need >32k we may need special infra.
[09:06] James Lee: for our triage assistant most prompts are <512 tokens, but sometimes long chart contexts are ~2k.
[09:12] Priya Nair: that's fine, we'll include a 2k token scenario in the matrix.
[09:16] Alex Johnson: quick aside: do you have any enterprise procurement/contract timeline constraints? we sometimes need an NDA before sharing some artifacts.
[09:25] Olivia Park: procurement: if POC goes well we expect procurement starting in June. we can do an NDA now if needed.
[09:31] Alex Johnson: we can send a mutual NDA and attach our standard security package.
[09:35] James Lee: ok. let's talk about measurable success criteria phrased simply so both teams agree. I'll read out what we discussed: 1) p95 latency <400ms for prompts <128 tokens on production-like config, 2) sustain 100 req/s with <1% error rate, 3) quality drop <2% vs baseline, 4) clear cost estimates for 1M tokens. any additions?
[09:54] Priya Nair: add: 5) streaming time-to-first-token under 200ms for interactive flows, 6) validated KV cache warm-up gives >20% token cost reduction for repeated sessions.
[10:08] Tom Wu: sounds good. question: for cost estimates do you provide breakdown across batching strategies?
[10:14] Alex Johnson: yes we'll show cost per request across batching profiles. we'll run batching sweeps to find the best cost-latency tradeoff for your workload.
[10:23] Maria Gonzalez: who will manage the harness in our VPC? will Redwood run it end-to-end or do we?
[10:30] Liam Ortiz: both options available. typically for initial runs Redwood runs the harness in your VPC with restricted creds; later you can own the harness. we provide deployment docs.
[10:39] Olivia Park: what credentials and network setup are required?
[10:42] Priya Nair: we need a service account with minimal egress to the model endpoint and a bucket for logs. we'll send a checklist.
[10:51] James Lee: ok, let's confirm deliverables and owners once more.
[10:55] Alex Johnson: deliverables: harness template + README (Alex), streaming/non-streaming example configs (Priya), sample dashboard and reporting (Liam), and security package + NDA (Sales). customers deliver: scripts, sample dataset, access for VPC tests.
[11:10] Olivia Park: good. on the topic of model variants, can we test an open model vs your curated model for cost comparisons?
[11:18] Priya Nair: yes we can include an open model baseline (e.g., small Llama variant or other open checkpoint) to show delta in quality and cost. we'll call out licensing considerations.
[11:28] Tom Wu: during tests, if we see quality regressions we want quick rollbacks to prior model; how are rollouts handled?
[11:35] Liam Ortiz: Redwood's rollout supports canary and A/B and automatic fallback; for the POC we'll keep it manual but can demo rollbacks.
[11:44] Maria Gonzalez: any advice on the initial load profile? we'd like something realistic that mirrors clinicians — bursts in morning hours and idle late nights.
[11:53] Priya Nair: create a variable load profile with peak ramps and background steady traffic; include userthink and session stickiness to emulate real clients. we can help craft it.
[12:03] James Lee: ok schedule wise — we share artifacts by Friday (2025-05-23), you run initial sanity tests over weekend, and full runs the following week?
[12:12] Alex Johnson: correct. we'll aim for full runs week of 2025-05-26.
[12:16] Olivia Park: are there any costs on our side for the POC infra?
[12:20] Alex Johnson: for hosted sanity checks no cost, for dedicated heavy runs we may ask the customer to cover cloud spend or use a Redwood trial credit — we'll include that in the pricing note.
[12:31] Tom Wu: small nit: token counting alignment — we use different tokenizers, how do you normalize cost?
[12:36] Priya Nair: we normalize to a common tokenizer (we'll share the tokenizer config) and compute cost per normalized token. include raw token counts as well.
[12:45] Maria Gonzalez: good. also retention of logs — we only need them for two weeks. can you support that?
[12:50] Liam Ortiz: yes retention is configurable; default is 30 days but can be reduced.
[12:55] James Lee: one more — in terms of reporting, can you produce a short executive summary focusing on cost/latency/quality tradeoffs?
[12:59] Alex Johnson: yes a one-page exec summary will be included.
[13:03] Olivia Park: fine. any other technical risks we haven't covered?
[13:07] Priya Nair: model quantization risks (possible quality drop), long-context memory pressure, and networking variability for VPC tests — we'll call these out.
[13:15] Tom Wu: thanks. let's confirm the acceptance checklist we can sign off on after runs.
[13:20] Alex Johnson: acceptance checklist draft: 1) tests executed per agreed matrix, 2) metrics captured (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost), 3) quality regression <=2%, 4) security checklist passed for VPC/KMS/SSO, 5) documented steps for reproducibility.
[13:38] Maria Gonzalez: that works.
[13:40] James Lee: ok last question: do you support streaming error injection and retry logic tests?
[13:46] Priya Nair: yes the harness can inject network errors and simulate partial responses and retries; we'll add that to the test plan.
[13:55] Olivia Park: perfect. shall we recap next steps?
[14:00] Alex Johnson: recap: Alex to email harness template and README by 2025-05-22; Priya to share streaming/config examples by 2025-05-27; James to provide scripts and sample data by 2025-05-23; schedule full run week of 2025-05-26; Sales to send pricing/credit note.
[14:18] James Lee: thanks everyone, we'll get artifacts over.
[14:21] Liam Ortiz: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and post links to the repo.
[14:26] Alex Johnson: great, thanks — meeting over.
